body:
I'm a new contributor to this repository, so take my analysis with a grain of salt.

I believe the root cause is that `ObjectDBProfilerPanel` communicates with the global "current" debugger (`EditorDebuggerNode::get_singleton()->get_current_debugger()`) rather than the specific debug session it belongs to.

When multiple instances are running, `setup_session` is called for each one, creating a separate `ObjectDBProfilerPanel` per session. But every panel's constructor connects to the breaked signal of whichever debugger happens to be "current" at
construction time, and all snapshot requests (`_request_object_snapshot`, `_begin_object_snapshot`, `handle_debug_message`, `receive_snapshot`) are sent through `get_current_debugger()` which returns whichever debugger tab is selected, not necessarily the one associated with that panel.

This causes the snapshot flow to break:

1. `_request_object_snapshot` disables the button and sets `awaiting_debug_break = true`
2. The break request goes to the wrong debugger (or the breaked signal is listened on the wrong one)
3. `_on_debug_breaked` never fires for this panel, so `_begin_object_snapshot` never runs
4. `receive_snapshot` never runs, so the button is never re-enabled

The button stays permanently stuck because nothing resets `awaiting_debug_break` or re-enables `take_snapshot` when the session stops. I'm not 100% sure why deleting the `.godot` folder fixes this, but it's likely due to how Godot performs state persistence in that directory.

I think the way to fix this is to have each `ObjectDBProfilerPanel` store and use its own reference to a `EditorDebuggerSession` (which is already available in `setup_session`) for all communication. Additionally, `set_enabled(false)` (called on session stop) should reset the snapshot state (`awaiting_debug_break`, `requested_break_for_snapshot`, `partial_snapshots`) so the button recovers if a session dies mid-snapshot.

I will attempt to get a PR submitted for this change. However, as noted above this is my first change so need to get the change implemented and tested first which may take some time.

I'm able to reproduce on 4.7 dev 3 and latest master v4.7.dev.custom_build [755fa449c]. I noticed some details while testing:

- The snapshot file is generated when you press the button of the first session, but only the last session tab will update to show it
- Just the button from the first session generate files, all other sessions doesn't work at all
- Even setting the amount of instances to a lower value than the previous run, the same amount of session tabs will appear, i'm not sure if this is desired as the last session tab will also allow to press the snapshoot button, even if nothing happens (no file is generated in this case)
- Setting the number of instances to 1 or disabling `multiple run instances` and restarting the editor fixes the issue, no need to delete .godot
- If you press other session snapshot button that's not the first and later press the first session snapshot button, two files will be generated (no matter the amount of other sessions you have pressed the snapshot) and have a chance of trigger these errors:

```
  ERROR: Signal 'process_frame' is already connected to given callable 'ObjectDBProfilerPanel::receive_snapshot' in that object.
  ERROR: ObjectDB Snapshot file is empty: user://objectdb_snapshots/2026-04-09_00-54-16_2.odb_snapshot
```
